note: This faulted.yaml contains TWO deliberate changes vs known_good. (a) PRIMARY FAULT — the one to identify: ApiHandlerFunction env DB_SECRET_ARN points to a wrong/nonexistent ARN instead of !Ref DbSecret. (b) SCENARIO SETUP — not itself the fault: ApiHandlerRole.secretsmanager:GetSecretValue Resource was widened from !Ref DbSecret to '*' so the wrong-ARN lookup surfaces as ResourceNotFoundException rather than AccessDeniedException (which would be indistinguishable from arch03_fault02_security). The IAM widening must NOT be scored as a missed fault — identification credit belongs to the DB_SECRET_ARN root cause.
valid_fixes: Restore ApiHandlerFunction env DB_SECRET_ARN to !Ref DbSecret so the Lambda references the real deployed secret (minimal functional fix; passes the functional test on its own — 1 file, 1 line)

Re-scope ApiHandlerRole secretsmanager:GetSecretValue Resource from '*' back to !Ref DbSecret as least-privilege hardening (optional for function, good security practice; not required to pass the functional test)
invalid_patches: Create a new secret at the wrong ARN path to match the bad reference
Grant secretsmanager:* on * to work around the scope
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_get_log_tail(ace-bench-stack-api-handler) → shows ResourceNotFoundException on the secret ARN
ace_get_environment_variables(ace-bench-stack-api-handler) → reveals DB_SECRET_ARN points to a nonexistent ARN
ace_get_stack_outputs(ace-bench-stack) → shows real DbSecretArn; comparing to env var confirms the ARN mismatch
observability_check: functional_test assertion 'order_created' (POST /orders returns 201) fails; Lambda logs show ResourceNotFoundException for the wrong secret ARN
observable_symptom: POST /orders returns 500 on every request. Lambda logs show a ResourceNotFoundException when attempting to retrieve the database credentials — the secret ARN in the Lambda environment does not correspond to any existing secret. The IAM role has correct GetSecretValue permissions and a valid secret with correct credentials does exist in the account.
root_cause: PRIMARY FAULT (the one to identify): the Lambda function's DB_SECRET_ARN environment variable points to a nonexistent secret ARN ('ace-bench-stack-db-secret-wrong') instead of the actual deployed secret (!Ref DbSecret). Secrets Manager raises ResourceNotFoundException on every invocation before a database connection is attempted. SCENARIO SETUP (not the fault to identify): the ApiHandlerRole secretsmanager:GetSecretValue Resource was deliberately widened from !Ref DbSecret to '*' so that the wrong-ARN lookup returns ResourceNotFoundException instead of AccessDeniedException; this makes the credentials fault behaviorally distinct from the IAM-permission fault (arch03_fault02_security). The IAM widening is intentional test scaffolding and is NOT itself a fault to find — the minimal correct fix is restoring DB_SECRET_ARN.
